source.version: Published version, The Annals of Statistics 52(6), 2024, pp. 2931–2955; DOI 10.1214/24-AOS2452

enumeration.method: Independent uppercase small-cap heading enumeration across main-text pages 1–24 and visual comparison of all six complete statements.

checks: Six original main-text Theorems 1–6 independently enumerated across pages 1–24. All formula constants, subparts, exponent regimes, fixed/growing client qualifications and the continuation of Theorem 4 were visually compared with the published PDF. Lemma 1 and Corollary 1 remain outside the theorem inventory; the external supplement is excluded.

39 original source entries preserve client/federated risks, weights and target, geometry and network, the full DFL recurrence, three averaging schemes, complete numbered assumptions, consensus/MSE constants, covariance and smooth/regression Hessian estimators, clipping and time segments, and the actual one-step correction. Nine auxiliary passages preserve required contextual bindings and original conventions.

Independent source-clause reconstruction gives 77 direct uses and 143 related-theorem connections. Theorem 5 retains v=2 and its printed assumption list; it does not acquire stochastic-Hessian Assumption 4.4 or the plug-in estimator. Theorem 6 uses the corrected alpha=1 PR estimator and the plug-in Hessian, without importing the regression estimator or downstream confidence procedure.

Nineteen source notes retain matrix-dimension conventions, endpoint and time-zero ambiguities, referenced conditional assumptions, derivative-variable and aggregate-noise bindings, cross-client sampling, window/segment and clipping conditions, scalar/matrix Hessian distinctions and the uppercase F_k notation in Theorem 6. Three unresolved source-ambiguity records remain explicit; none is represented as corrected or proven.

All 39 entries retain literal source keywords, original passage kinds/headings and source-specific selectors. All 143 connections have exact same-paper paths and explanatory source correspondence. Statements and all selectors were checked with the HTML renderer, while source quotations were preserved.

All six content JSONs reproduce byte for byte in a fresh empty directory. Seven retained scripts keep extraction and independent validation separate. Reproduction and structural checks do not replace the recorded visual source comparison.

This is a completed review of what the original main text states, not a proof certification. Explicit source ambiguities remain, including how later theorems inherit the conditional hypotheses of Theorem 2(ii). No missing joint-law, interiority, integer-segment, zero-index or inverse convention has been silently supplied.

source_notes.note: Page 4 defines J=d^{-1}*1_d*1_d^T, but the right-centering matrix in Theta_hat_t*(I-J) must act on K client columns. Page 6 explicitly uses K^{-1}*1_K*1_K^T. Preserve both source passages and record the dimension mismatch; do not silently replace d by K inside the quoted definition.

Assumption 2.1 permits rho=0, and Theorem 1 evaluates delta at rho^(1/tau) and its square, while its printed delta definition says a in (0,1). The following remark uses the natural a=0 interpretation. Preserve the open domain and document that extension separately.

Theorem 1 at t=tau invokes eta_floor((t-tau+1)/2)=eta_0 although Assumption 2.2 introduces the sequence for t>=1. An empty sum occurs for tau=1. Record these finite-index conventions rather than silently adding values.

The remark after Theorem 1 changes the order of delta arguments and calls it (14), although equation (14) is the curvature condition. Keep the theorem formula delta(t,a,tau) and distinguish the remark typo.

Assumption 3.4(ii) prints phi triple-prime at t and phi double-prime at u without a full relation or quantifier for t; it also omits an absolute value on the third derivative. Preserve the original condition and record its ambiguity rather than substituting a standard self-concordance definition.

Assumption 3.4 has alternative strong-convexity and bounded-domain generalized self-concordance cases. Do not require the bounded-domain assumptions jointly with the positive-mu case. Theorem 5 separately requires a bounded domain in all cases.

Theorems 3, 4 and 6 refer to assumptions of Theorem 2. Resolve the common assumptions and retain its part-(ii) conditional step-size restrictions as referenced context; inspect the source carefully before deciding their scope. Do not import its fixed-K almost-sure conclusion as a premise.

Theorem 5 explicitly uses v=2 and lists 3.3–3.4 without 3.2. It nevertheless assumes 4.1, described by the author as stronger smoothness. Preserve the printed list; do not insert an unstated numbered assumption merely to match the other theorems.

Page 3 specifies IID observations within each client, while the covariance aggregation on page 12 uses the no-cross-client-covariance formula. Check whether cross-client independence is explicitly stated elsewhere in the main text; record any missing joint-sampling premise rather than inventing it.

Assumption 4.2 mixes notation for aggregated noise epsilon(theta) and epsilon(theta;xi^k), though epsilon(theta) itself sums noises from all clients. Retain its original variables and record the binding issue.

Equation (22) uses gradients at local estimate theta_hat_t^k and data xi_t^k with t=0..T-1; the update (6) uses theta_hat_(t-1)^k and xi_t^k with t>=1. Retain the original covariance-estimator indexing and inspect the time-zero/data-reuse issue.

The trailing-window Hessian estimator (24) uses a(T) observations but only states that a is positive integer-valued and nondecreasing; a(T)<=T is not explicit. Its local temporal mean also reaches index zero when the window spans all observations. Preserve the formula and note any undefined early indices.

In (31), r1+r2+r3=T is imposed, but for alpha=1 the printed r1=T^(1-zeta)/C2 and r2=T/C3, r3=T/C4 with fixed constants cannot sum to T for all T. Integer rounding is also unspecified. Preserve the original formulas without silently changing constants or a segment.

Thresholded V clips eigenvalues to [delta,1/delta] for a small fixed delta>0. The source does not explicitly state a relation between that interval and the limiting spectrum in the theorem. Record that limitation rather than assuming clipping becomes asymptotically inactive.

The regression Hessian estimator Z*V^{-1} need not be symmetric at finite T. The later sandwich formula repeats its inverse without a transpose, as printed. Keep original formulas and distinguish an estimator definition from a claim of finite-sample symmetry.

Equation (33) uses lowercase f_k with a data argument, but Theorem 6 prints uppercase F_k(theta_K*;xi_t^k), although F_k was defined as a population risk with only a parameter argument. Preserve the printed theorem and record the apparent notation error separately.

Theorem 6 expansion has remainder O_p(sqrt(K/T)+1/sqrt(K)); its CLT consequence requires both K and T to diverge. Do not extend it to fixed K based on the PR theorem, which permits fixed K under a different step-size regime.

The external supplement contains algorithm summaries, proofs and sparse-network variants. Main-text algorithm definitions are available and should be used directly. Do not read supplement bodies or add their results to the main-text theorem inventory.

The target is defined by constrained minimization over closed convex Phi. The main-text definition does not separately state an interior-target or unconstrained-stationarity condition. Preserve the stated asymptotic normality and record this domain issue rather than silently assuming a zero gradient at every constrained minimizer.

ambient_resolution.T1: Resolve the assumptions cited through Lemma 1: network contraction, polynomial step sizes, gradient-noise moments with v=1, convex L-smooth risks and gradient heterogeneity. Lemma 1 supplies B_MSE and B_CE used in the theorem-local Q definition. Keep both parameter-domain branches, all three delta terms, the transformed rho and the finite t/tau range.
ambient_resolution.T2: Resolve the common numbered assumptions, spatial mean, target, matrix disagreement and derived curvature mu_Rd. Delta_t, c1/c2 and v1/v2 are bound inside the statement. Part (ii) has its own D/gamma/c0 hypotheses; part (iii) alone fixes K for almost sure convergence. Theorem 1 supplies the definition/context of c0, not a new assumption on the data beyond the stated rate.
ambient_resolution.T3: Resolve the common assumptions referenced from Theorem 2 and the explicit Assumptions 4.1–4.3, plus the joint PR average, H and S. Keep finite K or K=o(T^(2alpha-1)), alpha<1 and the uniform target bound. Later references to Theorem 2 leave the scope of its conditional part-(ii) step-size restrictions unstated; preserve that source context and mark the scope ambiguity, rather than rewriting the theorem. Do not impose fixed K.
ambient_resolution.T4: Resolve the same base assumptions, with stochastic-Hessian Assumption 4.4 replacing the population-Hessian Assumption 4.3. The theorem uses centered covariance estimates, the trailing-window smooth Hessian estimate and the resulting sandwich. Keep K*a(T)->infinity, both uniform target/gradient bounds and the upper-beta chi-square convention. Do not require each client Hessian estimate to be individually consistent.
ambient_resolution.T5: Use the printed list: network and step-size assumptions, noise moments with v=2, heterogeneity/curvature, stochastic-gradient smoothness and population-Hessian regularity. Preserve bounded Phi for both alpha regimes, the two client-growth rates and the thresholded regression Hessian. Theorem 5 does not list Assumption 3.2 or require stochastic losses to have Hessians. Its conclusion is convergence of expected Frobenius norm, not squared norm.
ambient_resolution.T6: Resolve the common Theorem 2 assumptions and explicit 4.1,4.2,4.4, but use alpha=1 and the corrected PR estimator in (33). Its gradient correction is averaged over local prior iterates and uses the smooth plug-in Hessian. Preserve uppercase F_k with a data argument in the printed expansion and the unresolved notation discrepancy. The final CLT requires K and T both diverging, K=o(T), and both displayed remainder terms.

review_limits: Registered published PDF, DOI 10.1214/24-AOS2452, 25 pages; source identity pinned.
Main text ends after Funding on page 24; the external supplement is excluded and page 24 evidence is clipped above its listing.
Review concerns extraction fidelity and source correspondence, not proof correctness. Referenced-hypothesis, joint-law, boundary/index and segment-allocation ambiguities remain explicit.
